Fault detection alone does not establish accurate circuit localization: disrupting computation can reveal sensitivity without identifying the mechanism. Zhang and Nanda show that corruption methods and evaluation metrics substantially change patching results; they recommend in-distribution symmetric token replacement and logit difference for their studied settings. Gaussian corruption can distort internal behavior, while probability-based metrics can obscure negative components. These are empirical defaults, not universal guarantees. [Towards Best Practices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042)

Known-circuit recovery provides stronger calibration. ACDC evaluates edge-level true/false-positive rates against previously analyzed circuits and Tracr programs with known implementations. Recovery depends strongly on corruption distribution and metric; even synthetic tasks can fail under one intervention and succeed under another. Human-derived reference circuits remain incomplete, so distinguish exact synthetic ground truth from provisional natural-model circuits. ACDC also includes reset-network experiments as negative controls. Recommended evaluation: report localization precision/recall or ROC curves, compare against random selections matched for size, and test irrelevant interventions alongside behavioral recovery. [ACDC](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/34e1dbe95d34d7ebaf99b9bcaeb5b2be-Paper-Conference.pdf)

Restoration and disruption answer different questions: clean-to-corrupted patches test contextual sufficiency; corrupted-to-clean patches test contextual necessity. AND-like dependencies can evade individual restoration tests; redundant OR-like paths can evade individual disruption tests. Joint patches and path patching therefore help test interactions and mediation. Recommendation inferred from this literature: prioritize known-path recovery, negative controls, and interaction tests; retain fault detection as a supporting check. Evaluate circuit faithfulness and completeness separately—reproducing behavior with retained components does not establish that every relevant mechanism was recovered. [Heimersheim and Nanda](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.15255v1)
